missions.title: Research Missions
missions.subtitle: Optional field research by raion
missions.pickerPrompt: Tap a chunk to start a research mission
missions.pickerSubtitle: Find 5 dogs in one chunk. Each earns escalating XP.
missions.allCompletedBody: You've passed every Tbilisi mission. Nice work.
missions.howItWorks: Each raion is split into walkable ~1.25 km chunks colour-tagged by raion. Pick one on the map. Every freshly logged dog inside the chunk earns escalating XP (10, 20, 30, 40, 50), up to 20 dogs per day. Hit 5 dogs total to pass and claim a +100 XP bonus.

tour.promptTitle: Welcome to The Street Dog App
tour.promptBody: A quick 4-step tour to show you how everything fits together. Takes about a minute.
tour.step1Body: Find one street dog each day to claim a +15 XP daily directive. The simplest way to keep your streak alive.
tour.step2Body: Every logged sighting bumps your XP. Brand-new dogs and new-to-you dogs earn more. Each 100 XP = a new researcher level.
tour.step3Body: Missions ask you to find 5 dogs inside one walkable chunk. Finishing one is worth +100 XP plus everything you earn for the sightings themselves.
tour.step4Body: Switch between every dog nearby, ones you found first, ones you've logged, and your favourites. Ready to start?

partnerClinics.intro: If the dog looks badly hurt, call ahead before bringing them in. Most clinics treat street dogs at a reduced rate or for free when the local rescue network is involved.
partnerClinics.firstAidTitle: How to help an injured street dog
partnerClinics.firstAidBody:
1. Approach slowly from the side, never head-on. Crouch and let the dog come to you.
2. Speak softly. Avoid sudden movements and eye contact.
3. If the dog is bleeding, apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth.
4. Do not give food or water if the dog is unconscious.
5. Call a partner clinic before transport so they're ready.
6. Wrap the dog in a coat or blanket to keep it warm and contained.

adopt.title: Adopting {name}
adopt.step1Body: Spend time with them in their usual area. Bring water and treats. Note their reaction to other dogs and people.
adopt.step2Body: Take the dog to one of the partner clinics for an initial exam, parasite screening, and vaccinations.
adopt.step3Body: Required: rabies, DHPPi, leptospirosis. The clinic implants an ISO microchip and registers it in your name.
adopt.step4Body: Recommended for every adopted street dog. Reduces wandering, marking, and prevents accidental litters.
adopt.step5Body: Quiet first week. Crate or safe corner, scheduled meals, slow introductions to other pets.
adopt.docsBody:
· Passport (yours)
· Vet certificate from the clinic
· Vaccination booklet with rabies dated within the last year
· Microchip registration in your name
· For international travel: EU pet passport (issued by the clinic) and a 30-day waiting period after rabies vaccination
